newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt press sceptical about Israel peace summit.
newsitem.headline: Egypt press sceptical about Israel peace summit.

text.p: Egyptian newspapers were sceptical about what could come from Tuesday's summit between Egypt and Israel and blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the crisis in Middle East peacemaking.

President Hosni Mubarak and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh on ways to restart Palestinian-Israeli peace talks stalled by conflicting views on Jewish settlements.

"Experience has taught us that we must be cautious when dealing with Israel's prime minister, not believe everything he says," Saeed Sonbol, a senior editor at the government-owned daily Al-Akhbar said in his daily column.
"We're not very optimistic about dealing with him because Netanyahu is the reason behind the deterioration in the peace process," he added.

Peace talks plunged into crisis in March after Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The Palestinians refuse to restart the negotiations until settlement building on land occupied by Israel in 1967 stops, a position which Egypt supports.

"Mr Netanyahu is fully aware of what is needed to solve the problem, and what is needed are not just Arab, Egyptian or Palestinian demands and it's nothing unusual either," the official al-Ahram daily said in an editorial.

"There's no room at the present time for dithering or complicated formulae. The solution is simple and easy... and failure this time will be a problem because the alternative is unknown," the editorial added.
Egypt, which made peace with the Jewish state in 1979, considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the peace talks and has often mediated between the Palestinians and Israel.
But since Netanyahu was elected last May, Cairo has taken the side of the Palestinians and officials have said Egypt would champion their stand in the meeting with Netanyahu.
The Israeli prime minister has been a target of ridicule, particularly in the Egyptian opposition press, since he refused to abide by peace formulae agreed upon by the previous government.
Al-Wafd opposition daily warned Netanyahu in a front-page editorial he had "pushed the region to the edge" and Arab patience had reached the end of its tether.

"Israel must know that this patience can turn sour and that Israel can lose a lot if it continues this intransigence...the whole situation can blow up in his face and Netanyahu will lose everything because no one in the world will accept his leading the region to the brink of war," the daily added.
